claims: C1 an instruction is misaligned when it conflicts with the letter of a higher-level instruction
C2 an instruction is misaligned when it conflicts with the implied intent of a higher-level instruction
C3 a Model Spec principle with user authority is overridden by an explicit developer or user instruction
C4 a Model Spec principle with guideline authority is overridden by an explicit or implicit developer or user instruction

concepts.name: misaligned_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that conflicts with the letter or implied intent of some higher-level instruction

concepts.name: applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that applies to the current request, determined by filtering candidate instructions
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is at authority level L
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of higher-level instructions, so each instruction must carry an authority level for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: instruction I is a higher-level instruction than instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'some higher-level instruction', so a relation between two instructions' levels must exist

concepts.name: conflicts_with_letter
concepts.gloss: instruction I conflicts with the letter of instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause distinguishes conflict with the letter from conflict with implied intent, so each needs its own relation

concepts.name: conflicts_with_intent
concepts.gloss: instruction I conflicts with the implied intent of instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause distinguishes conflict with implied intent from conflict with the letter, so each needs its own relation

concepts.name: user_authority_principle
concepts.gloss: I is a Model Spec principle with user authority
concepts.inference: the example distinguishes principles by their authority level, so a class for user-authority principles is needed

concepts.name: guideline_authority_principle
concepts.gloss: I is a Model Spec principle with guideline authority
concepts.inference: the example distinguishes principles by their authority level, so a class for guideline-authority principles is needed

concepts.name: explicit_developer_user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction stated explicitly by a developer or user, as opposed to one merely implied
concepts.inference: the example contrasts explicit with implicit instructions, so a class for explicit developer/user instructions is needed

concepts.name: developer_user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from a developer or user, whether stated explicitly or only implied
concepts.inference: the example contrasts explicit with implicit instructions, so a class for explicit-or-implicit developer/user instructions is needed

ontology.gloss: I is misaligned because it conflicts with the letter of a higher-level instruction J
I is misaligned because it conflicts with the implied intent of a higher-level instruction J

asserts.read_back: applying instruction % is forbidden because it is misaligned

closure.reason: the clause only forbids applying an instruction that is misaligned; it does not forbid applying any other instruction, so silence permits
